extracted.intended_audience: California state agency staff (rulewriters) and members of the public participating in California rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for California state agencies on complying with the Administrative Procedure Act (APA) and OAL rules when adopting regulations, and for the public to understand participation opportunities and procedural differences (regular vs emergency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with APA rulemaking procedures and OAL standards
rubrics_metrics.description: OAL is responsible for ensuring that California state agencies comply with the rulemaking procedures and standards set forth in California’s Administrative Procedure Act (APA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adopting regulations, every department, division, office, officer, bureau, board or commission in the executive branch of the California state government must follow the rulemaking procedures in the APA (Government Code section 11340 et seq.) and regulations adopted by the Office of Administrative Law (OAL), unless expressly exempted by statute from some or all of these requirements. The APA requirements are designed to provide the public with a meaningful opportunity to participate in the adoption of regulations or rules that have the force of law by California state agencies and to ensure the creation of an adequate record for the OAL and judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'regulation'
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'regulation' is any rule, regulation, order or standard of general application or the amendment, supplement, or revision of any rule, regulation, order, or standard adopted by any state agency to implement, interpret, or make specific the law enforced or administered by it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition determines what agency actions are subject to APA rulemaking requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of rulemaking process: Regular vs Emergency
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations subject to the APA are generally adopted through the 'Regular' or 'Emergency' rulemaking processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rulemaking process used by an agency to adopt regulations will dictate what procedural requirements must be followed, including but not limited to the contents of the rulemaking record, timeframes, opportunities for public participation, OAL’s review and effective dates for the regulations. For more information, follow the links to 'Regular Rulemaking Process' and 'Emergency Rulemaking Process.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the rulemaking record
rubrics_metrics.description: The rulemaking process used by an agency will dictate the required contents of the rulemaking record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not enumerated on this page, the record content is a procedural requirement tied to the process (regular vs emergency) and is essential to OAL review and to create an adequate record for judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframes for rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The rulemaking process determines applicable timeframes for actions in the adoption of regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must follow the timeframes associated with the chosen rulemaking process (regular or emergency); these affect public notice periods, comment deadlines, and effective dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunities for public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The APA requirements are designed to provide the public with a meaningful opportunity to participate in the adoption of regulations or rules that have the force of law by California state agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must provide notice and opportunities for public comment as required by the applicable rulemaking process; the extent and timing of public participation depend on whether the regular or emergency process is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: OAL review of adopted regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: OAL review is a necessary step in many rulemaking processes and the specifics are dictated by the process used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OAL reviews adopted regulations for compliance with the APA and OAL regulations; the review interacts with record content, public participation, and effective date determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates for regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The rulemaking process determines the effective dates for adopted regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective dates are set in accordance with statutory and procedural requirements tied to the chosen rulemaking path (regular vs emergency) and OAL review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory exemptions from APA requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may be 'expressly exempted by statute from some or all of these requirements.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a statute expressly exempts an agency or particular actions, those specific APA/OAL procedural requirements may not apply; agencies must identify and rely on the statutory exemption language when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underground regulations and petition process
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on underground regulations and the petition process is available on the OAL website under 'Underground Regulations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The existence of an underground-regulation petition process indicates an evaluative and remedial pathway for regulations or agency actions that may circumvent APA processes; agencies and the public can use the petition mechanism described by OAL.
